status_note: Comments due 11 Feb 2026; limited to electronic conspicuity and right-of-way
requirement_paraphrase: FAA reopened comments on electronic conspicuity and right-of-way because of disagreement over ADS-B Out/alternate devices and cost/practicality of detect-and-avoid; roughly 3,100 comments, over half on right-of-way.

edition_or_version: Draft/early published version, October 2020 presentation (not Ed. 3)
requirement_paraphrase: Slides describe a goal-based claim-argument-evidence structure; safety case must account for ODD violations; SPIs must show whether behaviour is safe, whether safety-case assumptions hold, and whether field data matches expectations; field alerts trigger root-cause fixes.

instrument: ICAO MID PBN SG/8 WP11 (UAE) GNSS anomalies
requirement_paraphrase: UAE reports GPS jamming affecting aircraft in the Emirates FIR (example 3 Oct 2023) and proposes updating state rules to require prompt action and mandatory reporting of interference, with ANSP reporting procedures.
Asks ICAO to alert States to GNSS interference and urges States to apply Doc 9849 three-step mitigation (monitor threats, assess risk, deploy mitigations).

instrument: ICAO MID CNS SG/14 WP05 (UAE) protecting surveillance data integrity against GNSS interference
edition_or_version: Dated 10 Oct 2025; meeting Abu Dhabi 19-23 Oct 2025
requirement_paraphrase: UAE reports an increase in interference cases and suspected spoofing over two years; asks the meeting to encourage MID States to set up surveillance-integrity investigation frameworks and designate national focal points for GNSS interference reporting, and to ask the ICAO MID Office to maintain a regional repository of reports.

instrument: ICAO MID CNS SG/15 WP08 (Saudi Arabia) national GNSS monitoring
requirement_paraphrase: Proposes a national GNSS signal monitoring and reporting system for the Jeddah FIR and a regional RFI database.
Describes a scenario-based safety evaluation process applied during ADS product development, for ADS on limited-access highways; excludes misuse, HMI and cybersecurity.

status_note: Published; stage 90.92 'to be revised'; confirmed 2022; ISO/DIS 12100.3 expected
requirement_paraphrase: Sets terminology, principles and methodology for risk assessment and risk reduction across machine life cycle, including documenting and verifying the process; basis for type-B and type-C standards. Excludes risk to domestic animals, property, environment.
Procedures and conditions for validating, by analysis and testing, specified safety functions, achieved category and achieved performance level of control parts designed under ISO 13849-1.

status_note: Published; stage 90.92 'to be revised' (2021-07-23), confirmed 2020; ISO/FDIS 13482 under development
requirement_paraphrase: Safety requirements for personal care robots (mobile servant, physical assistant, person carrier): inherently safe design, protective measures, user information. Earthbound only; excludes >20 km/h, toys, flying, industrial and medical robots.
Abstract notes that, at publication, no exhaustive internationally recognised data (e.g. pain or injury limits) existed for impact hazards such as collisions with personal care robots.
applies_to: Personal care robots with physical contact

status_note: Published; stage 90.92 'to be revised' (2025-06-26); to be replaced by ISO/AWI 15066-1
requirement_paraphrase: Technical specification for collaborative industrial robot systems and their work environment, supplementing collaborative guidance in ISO 10218-1/-2; not applicable to collaborative applications designed before its publication.

status_note: Published; ISO shows stage 90.92 'to be revised' (2024-07-08), ISO/DIS 26262-1 in development
requirement_paraphrase: Series scope: safety-related E/E systems in series-production road vehicles (excl. mopeds); excludes hazards such as electric shock or fire unless caused by E/E malfunction.

Methodology for design and integration of safety-related control parts, incl. software, for high-demand/continuous modes; does not define specific safety functions or required performance levels; excludes cybersecurity.

Safety requirements for industrial robots as partly completed machinery: inherently safe design, risk reduction, information for use. Not applicable to underwater, law-enforcement, military, airborne/space, medical/healthcare or prosthetic robots, to service robots where the public has access, or to consumer products; not retroactive to robots made before publication.
Safety requirements for industrial robot applications and cells across design, integration, commissioning, operation, maintenance, decommissioning and disposal, plus information needed at each stage.
applies_to: Integrators and users of robot cells
